bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷六十八 唐書44: 列傳20 薛廷珪 崔沂 劉岳 封舜卿 竇夢徵 李保殷 歸藹 孔邈 張文寶 陳乂 劉贊
title.en: Volume 68 Book of Later Tang 44: Biographies 20 - Xue Tinggui, Cui Yi, Liu Yue, Liu Ye, Feng Shunqing, Dou Mengzheng, Li Baoyin, Gui Ai, Kong, Miao, Zhang Wenbao, Chen Yi, Liu Zan
title.raw: 卷六十八 唐書44: 列傳20 薛廷珪 崔沂 劉岳 封舜卿 竇夢徵 李保殷 歸藹 孔邈 張文寶 陳乂 劉贊 Volume 68 Book of Later Tang 44: Biographies 20 - Xue Tinggui, Cui Yi, Liu Yue, Liu Ye, Feng Shunqing, Dou Mengzheng, Li Baoyin, Gui Ai, Kong, Miao, Zhang Wenbao, Chen Yi, Liu Zan

sentences.zh: 薛廷珪，其先河東人也。

translations.literal: Xue Tinggui—his ancestors were people of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tinggui was descended from a Hedong family.

sentences.zh: 父逢，咸通中為秘書監，以才名著於時。

translations.literal: His father Feng, in the Xiantong era served as Director of the Secretariat, and was famed in the time for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xue Feng served as Director of the Secretariat during the Xiantong reign and was renowned in his day for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 廷珪，中和年在西川登進士第，累曆台省。

translations.literal: Tinggui, in the Zhonghe era in Xichuan passed the jinshi examination, and successively served in offices of the Secretariat and Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui earned his jinshi degree in Xichuan during the Zhonghe reign and went on to hold a series of posts in the central secretariat and censorate.

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》：大順初，累遷司勳員外郎、知制誥。）〉

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang: early in Dazhun, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Old Book of Tang: in the early Dazhun period he rose through the ranks to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and imperial edict drafter.)〉

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In Qianning, he served as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning reign he served as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 駕在華州，改散騎常侍，尋請致仕，客遊蜀川。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Hua Prefecture, he was reassigned as Regular Attendant of the Palace Writing; soon afterward he requested retirement and traveled as a guest in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was at Hua Prefecture he was reassigned as Regular Attendant of the Palace Writing, then soon retired and lived as a guest in Shu.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，征為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong relocated to Luoyang, Tinggui was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》：光化中，復為中書舍人，遷邢部、吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。）〉

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang: in Guanghua he again served as Secretariat Drafter, was transferred to the two vice ministries of Punishments and Personnel, acted as supervisor of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Old Book of Tang: during Guanghua he returned as Secretariat drafter, rose to vice minister of both Punishments and Personnel, oversaw the Ministry of Rites examinations, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

sentences.zh: 時柳璨屠害朝士，衣冠畢罹其毒，廷珪以居常退讓獲全。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Can slaughtered court officials; the scholar-official class all suffered his poison, but Tinggui by his usual modesty and yielding preserved himself whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Can began slaughtering court officials, the entire scholar-official class fell victim to him, but Tinggui survived because his habitual modesty and restraint kept him out of harm's way.

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：朱全忠兼四鎮，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜。

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang: Zhu Quanzhong held four military commissions concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as bearer of the commission patent, and a guest officer saw him first and hinted that he should bow.
translations.idiomatic: (New Book of Tang: when Zhu Quanzhong held four commands at once, Tinggui arrived at Bian as bearer of the commission patent; a host officer met him first and hinted that he ought to bow.

sentences.zh: 廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎！

translations.literal: Tinggui pretended not to understand and said, "What virtue do I have that I would dare receive the Lord's bow!
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui feigned incomprehension and said, "What merit do I possess that I should accept a bow from Your Lordship!

sentences.zh: 」及見，卒不肯加禮。）〉

translations.literal: " When they met, he in the end refused to add the courtesy.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " When they finally met, he still refused to offer the expected courtesy.)〉

sentences.zh: 入梁為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Entering Liang, he became Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Liang service he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定河南，以廷珪年老，除太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, because Tinggui was old, he was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Tinggui was given the post of Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and retired on account of his age.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：廷珪與李琪嘗為太祖冊禮使。）〉

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi once served as envoys for the enfeoffment ritual for Taizu.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi had once served as ritual envoys at Taizu's enfeoffment.)〉

sentences.zh: 同光三年九月卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Tongguang 3.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 所著《鳳閣詞書》十卷、《克家志》五卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: His works Collected Writings from the Phoenix Pavilion in ten juan and Record of Honoring the Family in five juan were both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Writings from the Phoenix Pavilion in ten fascicles and Record of Honoring the Family in five fascicles both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 初，廷珪父逢，著《鑿混沌》、《真珠簾》等賦，大為時人所稱。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tinggui's father Feng composed the fu "Carving Chaos" and "Pearl Curtain," among others, and they were greatly praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui's father Feng had written fu such as "Carving Chaos" and "Pearl Curtain," which were widely admired in his day.

sentences.zh: 廷珪既壯，亦著賦數十篇，同為一集，故目曰《克家志》。

translations.literal: When Tinggui reached maturity, he also composed several dozen fu, gathered into one collection, and therefore it was titled Record of Honoring the Family.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinggui came of age he too wrote several dozen fu and collected them in one volume, which he titled Record of Honoring the Family.

sentences.zh: 崔沂，

translations.literal: Cui Yi,
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yi,

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·宰相世係表》：沂，字德潤。）〉

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Prime Ministers' Lineages: Yi, courtesy name Derun.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Prime Ministers' Lineages: Yi, styled Derun.)〉

sentences.zh: 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也。

translations.literal: He was the youngest son of Duke Wei of Wei, the prime minister Cui Xian, in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: He was the youngest son of Duke Wei Cui Xian, who served as prime minister during the Dazhong reign.

sentences.zh: 兄沆，廣明初亦為宰輔。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hang, early in Guangming also became a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Cui Hang also rose to chief minister in the early Guangming period.

sentences.zh: 沂舉進士第，曆監察、補闕。

translations.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor and Remonstrance Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yi earned his jinshi degree and served successively as investigating censor and remonstrance aide.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，累遷至員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhaozong, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose through the ranks to vice director and imperial edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 性抗厲守道，而文藻非優，嘗與同舍顏蕘、錢珝俱秉筆，見蕘、珝贍速，草制數十，無妨譚笑，而沂自愧。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upheld the Way, but his literary talent was not superior; once he drafted together with his colleagues in the office Yan Rao and Qian Xu, and seeing Rao and Xu swift and ample, drafting several dozen edicts without hindering conversation and laughter, Yi felt ashamed of himself.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and principled, but his literary gifts were not outstanding. Once, drafting edicts alongside his colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Xu, he watched them turn out dozens of documents with ease while chatting and laughing, and felt ashamed of his own pace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，謁國相訴曰：「沂疏淺，不足以供詞翰之職。

translations.literal: The next day he called on the chief minister and pleaded, "Yi is shallow and insufficient to fulfill the duties of literary drafting.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he visited the chief minister and said, "I am too shallow and unqualified for the work of drafting imperial prose.

sentences.zh: 」相輔然之，移為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: " The minister agreed and transferred him to Grand Master Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: " The minister agreed and reassigned him to Grand Master Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 入梁，為御史司憲，糾繆繩違，不避豪右。

translations.literal: Entering Liang, he became Director of the Censorate, correcting errors and restraining violations, not avoiding the powerful and great.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Liang service he became director of the censorate, correcting abuses and enforcing the law without fear of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 開平中，金吾街使寇彥卿入朝，過天津橋，市民梁現者不時回避，前導伍伯捽之，投石欄以致斃。

translations.literal: In Kaiping, the Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing entered court; passing Tianjin Bridge, the townsman Liang Xian did not withdraw in time, and the advance guard sergeants seized him and threw him against the stone railing, causing his death.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiping, Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing was entering court when he crossed Tianjin Bridge. A townsman named Liang Xian failed to clear the way in time; Yanqing's advance guards seized him and hurled him against the stone railing, killing him.

sentences.zh: 彥卿自前白於梁祖，梁祖命通事舍人趙可封宣諭，令出私財與死者之家，以贖其罪。

translations.literal: Yanqing went forward himself to report to the Liang Founder, and the Founder ordered the Palace Herald Zhao Kefeng to announce the decree, directing him to pay private funds to the dead man's family to redeem his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing reported the matter directly to the Liang Founder, who sent Palace Herald Zhao Kefeng to announce that Yanqing should pay compensation to the victim's family from his own purse to atone for the offense.

sentences.zh: 沂奏劾曰：「彥卿位是人臣，無專殺之理。

translations.literal: Yi submitted an impeachment saying, "Yanqing's position is that of a subject; there is no principle of unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted an impeachment stating, "Yanqing holds the rank of a subject and has no right to kill on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 況天津橋御路之要，正對端門，當車駕出入之途，非街使震怒之所。

translations.literal: Moreover Tianjin Bridge is a vital point on the imperial road, directly facing the Gate of Correct Deportment, on the route of the imperial carriage's coming and going—not a place for a street commissioner to vent his wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Tianjin Bridge lies on the imperial thoroughfare directly facing the Gate of Correct Deportment, along the very route of the imperial procession—it is no place for a street commissioner to vent his anger.

sentences.zh: 況梁現不時回避，其過止於鞭笞。

translations.literal: Moreover Liang Xian's failure to withdraw in time—his offense goes no further than flogging.
translations.idiomatic: As for Liang Xian's failure to clear the way in time, the offense warranted no more than a beating.

sentences.zh: 捽首投驅，深乖朝憲，請論之以法。

translations.literal: Seizing him by the head and casting him to his death deeply violates court law; I request that he be judged according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing a man and dashing him to his death is a grave breach of court law; I ask that the case be adjudicated under the code.

sentences.zh: 」梁祖惜彥卿，令沂以過失論，沂引鬥競律，以怙勢力為罪首，下手者減一等。

translations.literal: " The Liang Founder valued Yanqing and directed Yi to treat it as a case of negligence; Yi cited the statute on brawling, making reliance on power the chief offense and reducing the penalty one grade for those who carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The Liang Founder was reluctant to punish Yanqing and told Yi to treat the matter as negligence, but Yi invoked the statute on brawling, making abuse of power the primary offense and reducing the penalty by one grade for those who carried it out.

sentences.zh: 又鬥毆條，不鬥故毆傷人者，加傷罪一等。

translations.literal: Further, under the article on brawling and beating, one who beats and injures another without a prior fight adds one grade to the injury offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under the brawling statute as well, one who beats and injures another without provocation incurs an additional grade of punishment for the injury.

sentences.zh: 沂表入，責授彥卿遊擊將軍、左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: When Yi's memorial entered, Yanqing was demoted and appointed General of Mobile Campaign and Middle Commander of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's memorial was submitted, Yanqing was demoted to General of Mobile Campaign and Middle Commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 沂剛正守法，人士多之。

translations.literal: Yi was upright and upheld the law; scholars and officials greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's firm integrity and adherence to the law won wide admiration among the official class.

sentences.zh: 遷左司侍郎，改太常卿，轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and then moved to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, then became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，帶本官充西京副留守。

translations.literal: In Zhenming, while retaining his original office he served as Deputy Protector of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming he retained his ministerial rank while serving as Deputy Protector of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 時張全義留守、天下兵馬副元帥、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、中書令、魏王，名位之重，冠絕中外。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi was Protector, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Prefect of Henan, Administrator of the Six Armies and All Guard Units, Acting Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, and Prince of Wei—the weight of his titles and rank surpassed all within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Quanyi held the titles of Protector, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces, Prefect of Henan, Administrator of the Six Armies and All Guard Units, Acting Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, and Prince of Wei—his rank and prestige were unmatched at court or abroad.

sentences.zh: 沂至府，客將白以副留守合行廷禮，沂曰：「張公官位至重，然尚帶府尹之名，不知副留守見尹之儀何如？

translations.literal: When Yi arrived at the headquarters, the guest officer reported that the Deputy Protector ought to perform the court ceremony; Yi said, "Lord Zhang's official rank is extremely heavy, yet he still bears the title of Prefect—what is the protocol for a Deputy Protector meeting the Prefect?
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived at headquarters, the host officer informed him that the Deputy Protector was expected to perform the full court ceremony. Yi replied, "Lord Zhang's rank is exceedingly high, yet he still holds the title of Prefect—what is the proper protocol when a Deputy Protector meets the Prefect?

sentences.zh: 」全義知之，遽引見沂，勞曰：「彼此有禮，俱老矣，勿相勞煩。

translations.literal: " Quanyi learned of this, hurriedly received Yi in audience, and consoled him, saying, "Let us both observe propriety; we are both old—let us not trouble one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanyi heard of this and immediately received Yi in person, saying with courtesy, "Let us both observe proper form; we are both old men—there is no need to put each other to trouble.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗興復唐室，復用為左丞，判吏部尚書銓選司，坐累謫石州司馬。

translations.literal: " When Zhuangzong restored the Tang house, Yi was again employed as Left Vice Director and concurrently directed the Ministry of Personnel's selection office; through accumulated offenses he was demoted to Prefectural Military Adjutant of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhuangzong restored the Tang dynasty, Yi was reappointed Left Vice Director and put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection office, but was later demoted to military adjutant of Shizhou on account of accumulated offenses.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，召還，復為左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and again became Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong acceded, Yi was recalled and restored as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以衰疾告老，授太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: Citing age and illness, he requested retirement and was granted Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He cited age and illness to request retirement and was granted the title of Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒於龍門之別墅，時年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died at his villa at Longmen, at the age of over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his villa in Longmen at the age of over seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 劉嶽，字昭輔。

translations.literal: Liu Yue, courtesy name Zhaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue, styled Zhaofu.

sentences.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, and following Emperor Xiaowen's relocation to Luoyang they became people of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family resettled in Dai, and after Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang they became Luoyang natives.

sentences.zh: 八代祖民部尚書渝國公政會，武德時功臣。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhenghui, Duke of Yu, Minister of Revenue, was a meritorious minister in the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Liu Zhenghui, Duke of Yu and Minister of Revenue, was a meritorious minister of the Wude reign.

sentences.zh: 祖符，蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was Prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Fu served as Prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 父珪，洪洞縣令。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Magistrate of Hongdong County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Gui was magistrate of Hongdong County.

sentences.zh: 符有子八人，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Fu had eight sons, all of whom passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had eight sons, every one of whom earned the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 珪之母弟瑰、玕，異母弟崇夷、崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brothers by the same mother were Gui and Gan; younger brothers by a different mother were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brothers by the same mother were Liu Gui and Liu Gan; his half-brothers were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.

sentences.zh: 崇龜，乾寧中廣南節度使；

translations.literal: Chonggui, in Qianning was Military Commissioner of Guangnan;
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui served as Military Commissioner of Guangnan during Qianning;

sentences.zh: 崇望，乾寧中宰相；

translations.literal: Chongwang, in Qianning was prime minister;
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang served as prime minister during Qianning;

sentences.zh: 崇魯、崇謨、崇夷，並曆朝省。

translations.literal: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all successively served in the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all held posts in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 嶽少孤，亦進士擢第，曆戶部巡官、鄭縣簿、直史館，轉左拾遺、侍御史。

translations.literal: Yue was orphaned young; he too passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Touring Official of the Ministry of Revenue, Registrar of Zheng County, and Direct Historian of the History Office, then was transferred to Left Remonstrance Aide and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yue lost his father young. He too earned the jinshi degree and served successively as touring official in the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian in the History Office, before becoming Left Remonstrance Aide and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明初，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Early in Liang Zhenming, he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenming period of Liang he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 嶽為文敏速，尤善談諧，在職累遷戶部侍郎，在翰林十二年。

translations.literal: Yue wrote with quick facility and was especially skilled at witty conversation; while in office he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served in the Hanlin for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Yue wrote with quick facility and had a gift for witty conversation. While in office he rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and spent twelve years in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，隨例貶均州司馬，尋丁母憂，許自貶所奔喪，服闋，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, following precedent he was demoted to Prefectural Military Adjutant of Junzhou; soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother, was permitted to rush home from his place of demotion for the funeral, and after the mourning period ended was appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yue was demoted along with others to military adjutant of Junzhou. He soon entered mourning for his mother and was permitted to return from exile for the funeral; after the mourning period he was appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，曆兵部吏部侍郎、秘書監、太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Secretariat, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong acceded, Yue served successively as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Secretariat, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嶽文學之外，通於典禮。

translations.literal: Beyond his literary learning, Yue was versed in ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from his literary accomplishments, Yue was well versed in ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 天成中，奉詔撰《新書儀》一部，文約而理當，今行於世。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled a work called New Ceremonial Codes; the text was concise and the principles appropriate, and it circulates in the world today.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled the New Ceremonial Codes—concise in style and sound in principle—and it remains in use today.

sentences.zh: 子溫叟，仕至御史中丞。

translations.literal: His son Wensou rose in office to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Wensou rose to serve as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: （《國老談苑》云：劉溫叟方正守道，以名教為己任。

translations.literal: (Garden of Talks among Elder Statesmen states: Liu Wensou was upright and upheld the Way, taking the norms of teaching as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: (Garden of Talks among Elder Statesmen records that Liu Wensou was upright and principled, holding himself to the standards of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞，其母甚賢。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was famed for filial service to his mother, and his mother was very worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was renowned for filial devotion to his mother, who was a woman of great virtue.

sentences.zh: 初為翰林學士，私庭拜母，母即命二婢箱擎公服、金帶，置於階下，謂溫叟曰：「此汝父長興中入翰林時所賜也。

translations.literal: When he first became Hanlin Academician, he paid respects to his mother in the private quarters; his mother immediately ordered two maidservants to carry in chests holding official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps below, saying to Wensou, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first appointed Hanlin academician, he paid his respects to his mother at home. She had two maidservants bring out chests containing official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps, saying to Wensou, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin during the Changxing reign.

sentences.zh: 自先君子薨背以來，嘗懼家門替墜，今汝能自致青雲，繼父之職，可服之無愧矣！

translations.literal: Since your late father's passing, I have always feared the family's decline; now you are able on your own to reach the blue clouds and succeed to your father's office—you may wear them without shame!
translations.idiomatic: Since your father's death I have feared our family's decline. Now you have risen on your own merits to succeed to your father's post—you may wear these robes without shame!

sentences.zh: 」因欷歔掩泣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she sighed and sobbed, covering her face in tears.
translations.idiomatic: " She then sighed and wept, covering her face.

translations.literal: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed in grief, withdrew to a separate chamber, wore plain clothes and ate simple food, and mourned in remembrance for several days before then donning the robes; scholar-officials considered this proper ritual.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed in grief, then withdrew to a separate room where he wore plain clothes and ate simple fare in mourning for several days before donning the robes. Scholar-officials regarded this as proper observance of ritual.)〉

translations.literal: Feng Shunqing,
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shunqing,

sentences.zh: 據《新唐書·宰相世係表》，封氏世居渤海蓚縣。

translations.literal: According to the New Book of Tang, Tables of Prime Ministers' Lineages, the Feng clan for generations resided in Zhuo County, Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: According to the New Book of Tang's tables of prime ministers' lineages, the Feng clan had long resided in Zhuo County in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 舜卿，字讚聖，父敖，字碩夫，戶部尚書、渤海縣男。

translations.literal: Shunqing, courtesy name Zansheng; his father Ao, courtesy name Shuofu, was Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing, styled Zansheng, was the son of Ao, styled Shuofu, who served as Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai.

translations.literal: The Book of Tang has his biography.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Tang contains his biography.)〉

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為禮部侍郎，知貢舉。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was Vice Minister of Rites and supervised the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang service he served as Vice Minister of Rites and oversaw the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 開平三年，奉使幽州，以門生鄭致雍從行，復命之日，又與致雍同受命入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, on a mission to Youzhou, he took his student Zheng Zhiyong to accompany him; on the day of reporting back, he and Zhiyong together received appointment to enter the Hanlin as Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 3, while on a mission to Youzhou he took his student Zheng Zhiyong along. On the day they reported back, both men were appointed Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 致雍有俊才，舜卿雖有文辭，才思拙澀，及試五題，不勝困弊，因托致雍秉筆，當時譏者以為座主辱門生。

translations.literal: Zhiyong had outstanding talent; although Shunqing had literary skill, his creative thought was dull and sluggish, and when tested on five topics he could not bear the strain, so he entrusted Zhiyong to wield the brush; critics at the time regarded it as the examiner shaming his student.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyong was brilliantly talented, but although Shunqing had some literary skill his wit was slow and labored. When tested on five topics he could not manage the strain and had Zhiyong write for him. Contemporaries mocked this as an examiner disgracing his own student.

sentences.zh: 莊宗同光已來，累曆清顯。

translations.literal: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang onward, he successively held pure and eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang reign onward he held a series of prestigious central posts.

sentences.zh: 封氏自太和以來，世居兩製，以文筆稱於時。

translations.literal: The Feng clan from Taihe onward for generations held the two drafting offices and were famed in the time for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe reign the Feng clan had for generations held the two imperial drafting offices and were renowned for their literary talent.

sentences.zh: 舜卿從子渭，

translations.idiomatic: Shunqing's nephew Wei,

translations.idiomatic: (Tables of Lineages: Wei, styled Xisou.)〉

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛時，為翰林學士，舜卿為中書舍人，叔侄對掌內外製。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was Hanlin Academician while Shunqing was Secretariat Drafter; uncle and nephew jointly held the inner and outer drafting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wei served as Hanlin academician while Shunqing was Secretariat drafter—the uncle and nephew jointly controlled the inner and outer drafting offices.

sentences.zh: 從子翹，於梁貞明中亦為翰林學士。

translations.literal: His nephew Qiao, in Liang Zhenming also became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Qiao also became a Hanlin academician during Liang's Zhenming period.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為給事中，因轉對上言，以星辰合度，風雨應時，請御前香一合，帝親爇一炷，餘令於塔廟中焚之，貴表精至。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng, he served as Supervising Censor; on a rotating audience before the throne he submitted that the stars and constellations were in proper alignment and wind and rain came at the right seasons, requesting one measure of incense before the throne—the Emperor personally burned one stick, and ordered the remainder burned at pagodas and temples, honoring his utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he served as supervising censor. At a rotating audience before the throne he reported that the stars were in alignment and the seasons timely, and requested a measure of incense for the imperial presence. The emperor personally burned one stick and had the rest burned at pagodas and temples, honoring his utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 議者以翹時推名族，出朝苑，登瑣闈，甚有岩廊之望，而忽有此請，乃近諸妖佞耳，物望由是減之。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Qiao was at the time esteemed as a man of distinguished lineage, had come from Chaoyuan and entered the privy chamber, and had great prospect of serving in the hall of state—yet suddenly he made this request, which was akin to the various sorcerers and flatterers; public esteem for him was thereby diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators noted that Qiao came from a distinguished lineage, had risen from the Hanlin precinct to the privy chamber, and seemed destined for high office—yet this sudden request resembled the antics of sorcerers and sycophants, and his reputation suffered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 竇夢徵，同州人。

translations.literal: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少苦心為文，登進士第，曆校書郎，自拾遺召入翰林，充學士。

translations.literal: In youth he painstakingly devoted himself to writing, passed the jinshi examination, successively served as Proofreader, and was summoned from Remonstrance Aide into the Hanlin Academy as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he labored over his writing, earned the jinshi degree, served as proofreader, and was summoned from remonstrance aide into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，加兩浙錢鏐元帥之命。

translations.literal: In Liang Zhenming, the commission of Commander-in-Chief was conferred on Qian Liu of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang's Zhenming period the title of commander-in-chief was conferred on Qian Liu of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 夢徵以鏐無功於中原，兵柄不宜虛授，其言切直。

translations.literal: Mengzheng held that Liu had no merit in the Central Plains and that military authority should not be granted in vain; his words were sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzheng argued that Liu had rendered no service to the Central Plains and that military authority should not be granted without cause; his remonstrance was blunt and forthright.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以觸時忌，左授外任。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang, because he had touched a taboo of the time, demoted him and sent him to an external post.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had touched a political sore point, the Last Emperor of Liang demoted him to service outside the capital.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：竇以錢公無功於本朝，僻在一方，坐邀恩澤，不稱是命，乃抱麻哭於朝。

translations.literal: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: Dou held that Lord Qian had no merit to the present dynasty, sat remote in one region, and received favor without deserving it; the commission was unfitting, so he clutched the hemp mourning garb and wept at court.
translations.idiomatic: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: Dou argued that Lord Qian had done nothing for the dynasty, held a remote corner of the realm, and yet received honors he did not deserve. Deeming the appointment unworthy, he clutched the hemp mourning garb and wept at court.

sentences.zh: 翌日，竇謫掾於東州。）〉

translations.literal: The next day Dou was demoted to a staff post in the eastern prefecture.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dou was demoted to a staff post in an eastern prefecture.)〉

sentences.zh: 有頃，復召為學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗入汴，夢徵以例貶沂州，居嘗感梁末帝舊恩，因為《祭故君文》云：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Mengzheng was demoted by precedent to Yizhou; while living there he often felt gratitude for the old favor of the Last Emperor of Liang, and therefore composed an Elegy for the Former Lord, saying, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Mengzheng was demoted by precedent to Yizhou. Remembering the kindness the Last Emperor of Liang had shown him, he composed an Elegy for the Former Lord, which began: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 四海九州，天回眷命，一女二夫，人之不幸。

translations.literal: The four seas and nine provinces—Heaven turns its favoring mandate; one woman, two husbands—the misfortune of a person.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas and nine provinces—Heaven has turned its mandate; one woman, two husbands—what misfortune for a subject!

sentences.zh: 當革故以鼎新，若金銷而火盛，必然之理，夫何足競」云。

translations.literal: One ought to remove the old to renew the cauldron, as metal melts when fire blazes—this is inevitable principle; what is there to contend over?" he said.
translations.idiomatic: The old must give way to the new, as metal melts in a blazing fire—such is the way of things; why struggle against it?" he wrote.

sentences.zh: 秉筆者皆許之，尋量移宿州。

translations.literal: Those who wielded the brush all praised it; soon he was transferred by administrative discretion to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow writers all praised the piece, but he was soon transferred to Suzhou by administrative order.

sentences.zh: 天成初，遷中書舍人，復入為翰林學士、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Tiancheng he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, again entered service as Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tiancheng period he was promoted to Secretariat drafter and again entered the Hanlin Academy as academician and Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：竇失意被謫，嘗鬱鬱不樂，曾夢有人謂曰：「君無自苦，不久當復故職。

translations.literal: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: Dou, disheartened by demotion, was once gloomy and unhappy; he dreamed someone said to him, "Do not torment yourself—you will soon return to your former office.
translations.idiomatic: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: Demoted and disheartened, Dou grew despondent. He once dreamed that someone told him, "Do not torment yourself—you will soon return to your former post.

sentences.zh: 然將來慎勿為丞相，苟有是命，當萬計避之。

translations.literal: But in the future be careful never to become chief minister; if such a commission should come, you must by every means avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: But hereafter beware of becoming chief minister; if such an appointment should come, you must do everything possible to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 」其後竇復居禁職。

translations.literal: " Afterward Dou again held a restricted office.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Dou returned to a restricted palace post.

sentences.zh: 有頃，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 竇忽憶夢中所言，深惡其事。

translations.literal: Dou suddenly recalled what had been said in the dream and deeply dreaded the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Dou suddenly remembered the dream and deeply dreaded what it foretold.

sentences.zh: 然已受命，不能遜避，未幾果卒。）〉

translations.idiomatic: Yet he had already accepted the appointment and could not escape it; before long he died as the dream had warned.)〉

sentences.zh: 夢徵隨計之秋，文稱甚高，尤長於箋啟，編為十卷，目曰《東堂集》，行於世。

translations.literal: In the autumn when Mengzheng went up for the examination, his literary reputation was very high; he was especially skilled at letters and memorials, compiled into ten juan under the title Eastern Hall Collection, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengzheng went up for the examinations his literary reputation was very high. He excelled especially at letters and memorials, which were collected in ten fascicles under the title Eastern Hall Collection and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 李保殷，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 昭宗朝，自處士除太子正字，改錢塘縣尉。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, from Recluse Scholar he was appointed Proofreader to the Crown Prince, then changed to Prefectural Assistant of Qiantang County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose from recluse scholar to proofreader to the crown prince, then became assistant prefect of Qiantang County.

sentences.zh: 浙東帥董昌辟為推官，調補河府兵曹參軍，曆長水令、《毛詩》博士，累官至太常少卿、端王傅。

translations.literal: The Zhedong commander Dong Chang recruited him as investigating officer; he was transferred and appointed Military Staff Officer of the He Prefecture headquarters, successively served as Magistrate of Changshui and Doctor of the Mao Odes, and by accumulated promotion reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Tutor to the Prince of Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhedong commander Dong Chang recruited him as investigating officer. He was transferred to military staff officer at the He Prefecture headquarters, served as magistrate of Changshui and doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and tutor to the Prince of Duan.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，撰《刑律總要》十二卷；

translations.literal: He entered service as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Law in twelve juan;
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Law in twelve fascicles;

sentences.zh: 與兵部侍郎郗殷象論刑法事。

translations.literal: together with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang he debated matters of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: and together with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang debated matters of penal law.

sentences.zh: 左降房州司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Prefectural Military Adjutant of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to military adjutant of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 同光初，授殿中監，以其素有明法律之譽，拜大理卿；

translations.literal: Early in Tongguang he was appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service; because he had long had a reputation for understanding law, he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongguang period he was appointed director of the Palace Domestic Service and, on account of his long-standing reputation for legal expertise, was made director of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 未滿秩，屬為人所製。

translations.literal: before completing his term, he happened to be framed by others.
translations.idiomatic: but before completing his term he was framed by others.

sentences.zh: 保殷曰：「人之多辟，無自立辟。

translations.literal: Baoyin said, "When many people have offenses, do not create offenses for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin said, "When many people commit offenses, do not manufacture offenses for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」乃謝病以歸，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home, and died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pleaded illness and retired home, dying at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 孔邈，文宣王四十一代孫。

translations.literal: Kong Miao was the forty-first-generation descendant of the Cultured Propagator King.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Miao was the forty-first-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺餘，神氣溫厚。

translations.literal: His body was over seven chi in height, and his bearing was warm and generous.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over seven chi tall, with a warm and dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，曆校書郎、萬年尉，充集賢校理，為諫議大夫，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Proofreader, Assistant Magistrate of Wannian, and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he became Grand Master Remonstrance and retired on account of old age.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the jinshi degree and served successively as proofreader, assistant magistrate of Wannian, and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies before becoming grand master remonstrance and retiring on account of age.

sentences.zh: （案：《孔邈傳》，原本殘闕。

translations.literal: (Note: the Biography of Kong Miao in the original text is defective.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the original Biography of Kong Miao is defective.

sentences.zh: 考《冊府元龜》云：乾寧五年，登進士第，除校書郎。

translations.literal: Examining the Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace, it states: in the fifth year of Qianning he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace, he passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Qianning and was appointed proofreader.

sentences.zh: 崔遠在中書，奏為萬年尉，充集賢校理，以親舅獨孤損方在廊廟，避嫌不赴職。）〉

translations.literal: Cui Yuan was in the Secretariat and memorialized appointing him Assistant Magistrate of Wannian and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was then in the hall of state, he avoided the conflict of interest and did not take up the post.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, then in the Secretariat, memorialized appointing him assistant magistrate of Wannian and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was serving at court he declined the post to avoid conflict of interest.)〉

sentences.zh: 張文寶，昭宗朝諫議大夫顗之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Master Remonstrance Yi of the Zhaozong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Master Remonstrance Yi, who served under Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 文寶初，依河中朱友謙為從事。

translations.literal: Early in Wenbao's career, he relied on Zhu Youqian of Hezhong as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career Wenbao served on the staff of Zhu Youqian at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以文寶知制誥，曆中書舍人、刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍、知貢舉，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made drafter of edicts and successively served as Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Writing, and supervisor of the examination, then was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made imperial edict drafter and served successively as Secretariat drafter, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Writing, and supervisor of the examinations before becoming Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 文寶性雅淡稽古。

translations.literal: Wenbao's nature was refined, restrained, and devoted to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao was refined and scholarly by nature, with a deep devotion to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 長興初，奉使浙中，泛海船壞，水工以小舟救，文寶與副使吏部郎中張絢信風至淮南界，偽吳楊溥禮待甚至，兼厚遺錢幣、食物。

translations.literal: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhejiang, his seagoing vessel was wrecked; sailors rescued them in small boats. Wenbao and the deputy envoy, Director in the Ministry of Personnel Zhang Xuan, trusted the wind and reached the border of Huainan; the false Wu ruler Yang Pu treated them with the utmost courtesy and also generously bestowed money and food.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Changxing period, while on a mission to Zhejiang, his ship was wrecked at sea and sailors rescued the party in small boats. Wenbao and his deputy, Director in the Ministry of Personnel Zhang Xuan, drifted on the wind to the Huainan border, where the Wu ruler Yang Pu received them with great courtesy and generously bestowed money and provisions.

sentences.zh: 文寶受其食物，反其錢幣，吳人善之，送文寶等復至杭州宣國命，還青州，卒。

translations.literal: Wenbao accepted their food but returned their money; the Wu people approved of this and sent Wenbao and the others on to Hangzhou to announce the imperial commission, then returned to Qingzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao accepted the food but returned the money, which the Wu people admired. They escorted Wenbao and his party to Hangzhou to deliver the imperial commission, then sent them back toward Qingzhou, where Wenbao died.

sentences.zh: 子吉，嗣位邑宰。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded to the post of district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded to the post of district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 劉讚，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文性。

translations.literal: In youth he had a literary disposition.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed a literary bent.

sentences.zh: 父比，為令錄，誨以詩書，夏月令服青襦單衫。

translations.literal: His father Bi served as a county clerk and instructed him in poetry and books; in summer months he ordered him to wear a blue jacket and single-layer shirt.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi served as a county clerk and tutored him in the classics. In summer he made the boy wear a plain blue jacket and single-layer shirt.

sentences.zh: 比每肉食，別置蔬食以飯讚，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也。

translations.literal: Whenever Bi ate meat, he set aside plain vegetable food for Zan's meal and told him, "Meat is the salary of a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Bi ate meat he set aside a plain vegetable meal for Zan and told him, "Meat is an official's perquisite.

sentences.zh: 爾欲食肉，當苦心文藝，自可致之，吾祿不可分也。

translations.literal: If you wish to eat meat, you must painstakingly devote yourself to literary arts—you can obtain it yourself; my salary cannot be shared.
translations.idiomatic: If you want to eat meat, you must earn it through your own literary effort. My salary is not yours to share.

sentences.zh: 」由是讚及冠有文辭，年三十餘登進士第。

translations.literal: " From this Zan, by the time he came of age, had literary skill; in his thirties he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: " Under this training Zan developed literary skill by the time he came of age and earned his jinshi degree in his thirties.

sentences.zh: 魏州節度使羅紹威署巡官，罷歸京師，依開封尹劉鄩。

translations.literal: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer; when dismissed he returned to the capital and relied on Kaifeng Prefect Liu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer. When that post ended he returned to the capital and attached himself to Kaifeng Prefect Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 久之，租庸使趙岩表為巡官，累遷至戶部員外郎，職如故。

translations.literal: After a long time, Transport and Corvée Commissioner Zhao Yan memorialized appointing him touring officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, his duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Transport and Corvée Commissioner Zhao Yan recommended him as touring officer, and he rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue while keeping the same duties.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，租庸副使孔謙以讚里人，表為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Transport and Corvée Commissioner Kong Qian, being a fellow townsman of Zan, memorialized appointing him Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Transport and Corvée Commissioner Kong Qian, a fellow townsman, recommended Zan as salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天成中，曆知制誥、中書舍人。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he successively served as drafter of edicts and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he served successively as imperial edict drafter and Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 與學士竇夢徵同年登第，鄰居友善，夢徵卒，讚與同年楊凝式緦麻為位而哭，其家無嫡長，與視喪事，恤其孀稚，人士稱之。

translations.literal: He and Academician Dou Mengzheng passed the examination in the same year and were neighbors on friendly terms; when Mengzheng died, Zan and his examination-year colleague Yang Ningshi set up a hemp-mourning station and wept; the family had no eldest son of the main line, so he oversaw the funeral affairs and cared for the widow and young children—scholars and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Hanlin academician Dou Mengzheng had passed the examinations in the same year and were friendly neighbors. When Mengzheng died, Zan and his examination-year colleague Yang Ningshi set up a mourning station in hemp garb and wept. With no eldest son in the family, Zan oversaw the funeral and cared for the widow and children, winning praise from the official class.

sentences.zh: 改御史中丞、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 讚性雍和，與物無忤，居官畏慎，人若以私幹之，雖權豪不能移其操。

translations.literal: Zan's nature was mild and harmonious; he clashed with nothing and no one. In office he was cautious and careful; if people tried to approach him with private requests, even the powerful and great could not move his principles.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was mild and even-tempered, clashing with no one. In office he was cautious and scrupulous; even the powerful could not sway him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改秘書監，兼秦王傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Director of the Secretariat and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: （《冊府元龜》：秦王為元帥，秦王府判官、太子詹事王居敏與讚鄉曲之舊，以秦王盛年自恣，須朝中選端士納誨，冀其稟畏，乃奏薦讚焉。）〉

translations.literal: (Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace: the Prince of Qin was commander-in-chief; the Prince of Qin's headquarters adjutant and Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Wang Jumin was an old acquaintance from the same district as Zan. Because the Prince of Qin in the prime of youth was self-indulgent, upright men from court needed to be selected to offer instruction, hoping he would receive and fear them—therefore he memorialized recommending Zan.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace: when the Prince of Qin served as commander-in-chief, his headquarters adjutant and Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Wang Jumin, an old acquaintance of Zan's from the same district, recommended Zan because the young prince was self-indulgent and needed upright court officials to instruct him.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚節概貞素，忽聞其命，掩泣固辭，竟不能止。

translations.literal: Zan's integrity and character were pure and plain; suddenly hearing of the commission, he covered his face and wept and firmly declined, but in the end could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was a man of upright and unadorned character. When he heard of the appointment he wept and firmly declined, but could not refuse it.

sentences.zh: （案《通鑒》：瓚自以左遷，泣訴，不得免。

translations.literal: (According to the Comprehensive Mirror: Zan regarded it as a demotion, wept and pleaded, but could not be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Zan regarded the appointment as a demotion, wept and pleaded, but could not be released from it.

sentences.zh: 胡三省注云：唐制，六部侍郎除吏部之外，餘皆從四品下；

translations.literal: Hu Sanxing's note states: under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the Six Ministries, except Personnel, were all lower fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing notes: under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries, except Personnel, ranked at lower fourth grade;

sentences.zh: 王傅從三品。

translations.literal: a prince's tutor was upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: a prince's tutor ranked at upper third grade.

sentences.zh: 然六部侍郎為向用，王傅為左遷，以職事有閑劇之不同也。

translations.literal: Yet a vice minister of the Six Ministries was one in active use, while a prince's tutor was a demotion, because the duties differed in leisure and urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a vice ministry post was one of active responsibility, while a prince's tutorship counted as a demotion because the duties differed in importance and urgency.

sentences.zh: 當是時，從榮地居儲副，則秦王傅不可以閑官。

translations.literal: At that time Congrong's position was that of heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor could not be treated as an idle post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Congrong held the position of heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor could hardly be considered an idle post.

sentences.zh: 言蓋以從榮輕佻峻急，恐豫其禍，故求脫耳。）〉

translations.literal: The words probably meant that Congrong was frivolous, sharp, and harsh, and he feared being caught up in the disaster—therefore he sought to escape it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The comment probably means that Congrong was frivolous and harsh-tempered, and Zan feared being caught up in his downfall—hence his attempt to escape the appointment.)〉

sentences.zh: 時秦王參佐，皆新進小生，動多輕脫，每稱頌秦王功德，阿意順旨，隻奉談笑，惟讚從容諷議，必獻嘉言。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qin's staff were all newly risen young men, often frivolous and unrestrained; they constantly praised the prince's merit and virtue, flattered his wishes, and only offered banter—only Zan, with composure, offered indirect remonstrance and always presented good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's staff were all newly risen young men, often frivolous and unrestrained. They constantly flattered the prince's virtues and offered nothing but agreeable chatter—only Zan, with composure, offered indirect remonstrance and always gave sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 秦王常接見賓僚及遊客，於酒筵之中，悉令秉筆賦詩。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin often received guests, staff, and visitors; amid wine banquets he would have them all take up the brush and compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin often received guests and staff at wine banquets and required everyone present to compose poetry on the spot.

sentences.zh: （《冊府元龜》：時從榮溺於篇章，凡門客及通謁遊士，必坐於客次，自出題目，令賦一章，然後接見。）〉

translations.literal: (Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace: at the time Congrong was immersed in literary composition; all retainers and visiting scholars had to sit in the guest hall while he set the topic himself, ordering them to compose one piece, and only then would he receive them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Prime Tortoise of the Archive Palace: Congrong was obsessed with literary composition. Every retainer and visiting scholar had to wait in the guest hall while he set a topic and required a poem before granting an audience.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚為師傅，亦與諸客混，然容狀不悅。

translations.literal: Zan as tutor was also mixed among the various guests, yet his expression showed displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: As tutor, Zan was lumped in with the other guests, but his expression showed clear displeasure.

sentences.zh: 秦王知其意，自是戒典客，讚至勿通，令每月一度至衙。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin understood his meaning; from then on he warned the reception officer that when Zan came he was not to be admitted, ordering him to come to the headquarters only once a month.
translations.idiomatic: The prince understood his displeasure and instructed the reception officer not to admit Zan except for one monthly visit to headquarters.

sentences.zh: （《言行龜鑒》載：劉讚諫秦王曰：「殿下宜以孝敬為職，浮華非所尚也。

translations.literal: (Mirror of Words and Conduct records: Liu Zan remonstrated with the Prince of Qin, saying, "Your Highness ought to make filial piety and respect your duty; frivolity and display are not what should be honored.
translations.idiomatic: (Mirror of Words and Conduct records that Liu Zan remonstrated with the Prince of Qin: "Your Highness should make filial piety and respect your chief duty; frivolity and display are not worthy pursuits.

sentences.zh: 」秦王不悅，戒閽者後弗引進。）〉

translations.literal: " The Prince of Qin was displeased and warned the gatekeepers thereafter not to admit him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " The prince was displeased and told the gatekeepers never to admit him again.)〉

sentences.zh: 讚既官係王府，不敢朝參，不通慶吊，但閉關喑嗚而已，及秦王得罪，或言讚止於朝降，而讚已服麻衣備驢乘在門矣。

translations.literal: Zan, since his office was tied to the princely house, did not dare attend court audience, sent no congratulations or condolences, but only secluded himself in silent grief; when the Prince of Qin fell from grace, some said Zan would merely bow at court in submission—but Zan had already put on hemp garments and prepared donkeys and carriage at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bound to the princely household, Zan no longer attended court or exchanged congratulations and condolences, secluding himself in silent grief. When the Prince of Qin fell from grace, some said Zan would merely submit at court—but he had already donned hemp mourning garb and prepared donkeys and a carriage at his gate.

sentences.zh: 聞其言曰：「豈有國君之嗣，一旦舉室塗地，而賓佐朝降，得免死，幸也。

translations.literal: Hearing this he said, "How could there be an heir of the ruler's house whose entire household is suddenly wiped out, while a staff member merely bows in submission at court and considers escaping death good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this he said, "When an heir of the ruler's house is suddenly destroyed, how can a staff member merely bow in submission at court and call escaping death good fortune?

sentences.zh: 」俄而台史示敕，長流嵐州，即時赴貶所。

translations.literal: " Soon the censorate clerk showed the decree: he was exiled far to Lanzhou, and he immediately went to the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the censorate delivered the decree exiling him to Lan Prefecture, and he set out at once for his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 在嵐州逾年，清泰二年春，詔歸田里。

translations.literal: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in the spring of the second year of Qingtai an edict ordered him to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in Lan Prefecture, in the spring of Qingtai 2 an edict permitted him to return home.

sentences.zh: 妻紇幹氏塗中卒，讚比羸瘠，慟哭殆絕，因之亦病，行及石會關而卒，時年六十餘。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Gegan, died on the road; Zan by then was emaciated, wailed until nearly dead, and fell ill from this; traveling as far as Shihui Pass he died, at the age of over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Gegan, died on the journey. Already emaciated, Zan wailed until he nearly collapsed and fell ill. He died at Shihui Pass at the age of over sixty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自唐祚橫流，衣冠掃地，苟無端士，孰恢素風。

translations.literal: The historian says: Since the Tang mandate flowed askew and the scholar-official class was swept away, if there were no upright men, who could restore the pure style?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: After the Tang dynasty fell into turmoil and the scholar-official class was swept away, without upright men who could have restored the old standards?

sentences.zh: 如廷珪之文學，崔沂之剛正，劉嶽之典禮，舜卿之掌誥，洎夢徵而下，皆蔚有貞規，無虧懿範，固可以為搢紳之圭表，聳朝廷之羽儀，以之垂名，夫何不韙。

translations.literal: Such as Tinggui's literary learning, Yi's uprightness, Yue's ceremonial mastery, and Shunqing's holding of the drafting brush—down to Mengzheng and those below—all abundantly possessed upright standards and did not fall short of fine exemplars; they could indeed serve as models for the girdled and sashed, and as feathered banners for the court. To leave their names to posterity—what could be more fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Tinggui in literary learning, Yi in uprightness, Yue in ceremonial mastery, and Shunqing in imperial drafting—and from Mengzheng downward—all upheld upright standards without blemish on their fine reputations. They could serve as models for the official class and ornaments of the court. To leave such names to posterity—what could be more fitting?
